top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for a bounded, identifiable invention, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, and its realisation at 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, which independent laboratories have reproduced and intercompared. The overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes is a real reservation, but the lattice scheme is a distinct step if the citation is tied to the concept and its realisation and not to a record number or the pending redefinition of the second. A well-attributed mature award is better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for Katori, Ye or the optical clock community; my DFT and DMFT work is closer to other shortlisted candidates, which are not on this slate
